correctness.rationale: Reconstructed bijection between a plane tree with a marked full fringe occurrence and a smaller plane tree with one marked leaf, with exact m=n-k+1 vertex and ell-1 leaf increments. Narayana formulas give the Palm histogram and moments. The explicit adjacent-ratio product factors are both strictly decreasing for each j, proving log-concavity on all finite positive supports; n>=k+1 ensures at least one proper upper-tail deficit. Boundary m=2,3 treated. Variance yields covariance regression and complete integer sign cases. Standalone exact enumeration and fraction checks passed. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a natural binary decision problem — whether a Catalan tree was sampled normally or enriched by the number of occurrences of a specified fringe shape — the result identifies the optimal leaf-count statistic geometry *uniformly over every shape and tree size*. Enrichment is usually associated with directional count shifts, yet here for leaf-rich patterns both tails are suppressed and only a middle interval favors enrichment. This is a complete motivated structural likelihood-ratio classification, rather than a one-off numerical covariance, and the sharp finite-size zero criterion is complementary.
